- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overshoot, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for volatility decay.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% upward bias to correct for mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, avoid large swings; cap forecast volatility within ±3% of recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 3 days, assume lagged reaction; adjust forecast to align with 7-day moving average.
